prompt: Parse an HH:mm string, add a number of minutes (possibly negative, wrapping across midnight), and format the result back as HH:mm.
explanation: LocalTime.parse reads ISO HH:mm strings directly, and plusMinutes wraps around midnight in both directions -- 23:30 plus 45 minutes is 00:15, and negative amounts subtract time. Formatting back out uses DateTimeFormatter.ofPattern("HH:mm"), where the double HH keeps the leading zero so five past midnight prints as 00:05.
hints: java.time.LocalTime.parse("23:30") needs no explicit formatter -- HH:mm is the ISO local-time format.
plusMinutes already wraps past midnight and accepts negative values; no manual arithmetic is needed.
Format the result with DateTimeFormatter.ofPattern("HH:mm", java.util.Locale.US) so single-digit hours keep their leading zero.
